b: If you want to rest more, you probably need to rest more. Saving rest for when you think you’ve earned it or deserved it isn’t working anymore. It’s time to put rest first.

As adults (especially women), we tend to overdo it. We do way too much and rest way too little. Chances are, you rest when you are exhausted, sick or completely depleted. But until then, it’s go, go, go. I used to do the same thing and eventually my body said, “no thank you.”

After I was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2006, I finally started to listen to my body when it told me to slow down. I began doing less, stressing less and resting more. Eventually, I had more energy but I didn’t start doing more. Even though I had the capacity to get more done, I lost interest in wearing myself out in the name of being more productive.
5 Spaces to Clear If You Simply Want to Rest More
There are so many reasons to simplify your life but if you simply want to rest more, start with the following five spaces. Give attention to each space and keep making room to take care.
1. Clear your mind to make room for rest.

You don’t need an empty mind to rest but to enjoy it without the guilt of not getting other things done, you need to shift your thoughts. You may also need to shift your thoughts about how you measure your self-worth. If it’s directly connected to your productivity, to how much you get done, it will be hard to stop and rest. It will be helpful to remember this. Doing more things doesn’t make you a better person. It makes you a tired person.

If you want to rest more but a busy mind is getting in the way, consider these suggestions to slow your racing mind. Meditation and mindfulness can help but there are other ways to quiet things down in there.
2. The next space to clear is your calendar.

Make room on your calendar to rest consistently instead of waiting until you don’t have a choice. Your version of rest may be an actual nap or time to chill on the couch with some relaxing music. Scheduling time on your calendar will ensure that it happens. Treat it like an important appointment. In Gentle, Rest More, Stress Less and Live The Life You Actually Want you can learn more about how to put rest first.
3. If you want to rest more clear out some clutter.

Clutter gets in the way of your ability to wind down and to enjoy a healthier life. The longer you hold on to your clutter, the harder it may feel to let it go. Today is a great day to make the decision to live with less clutter. You don’t need to declutter everything overnight, but step by step, you can begin to trade your clutter for time, energy and peace of mind.

If you only have 20 minutes to rest, you don’t want to spend 10 minutes cleaning up clutter and getting ready to rest. Literally make space to rest by removing clutter from your home. Start with one small space. Make just enough clutter-free space to relax. These decluttering methods can help and here’s a list of things to declutter to help you get started.
4. Clear space between you and your phone.

Scrolling on your phone may feel restful, but it’s often stressful and will disturb your rest. Consider hiding your phone or at least turning on Do Not Disturb so you aren’t on high alert while you are trying to rest. If you like the space you create between you and your phone, here are some other gentle ways to break up with your phone.

Dr. Sahib Khalsa, a neuroscientist and psychiatrist at the Laureate Institute for Brain Research, explained in an interview that “technology can distract us from noticing important signals from the brain — and it can also be the source of our distress. We can scroll for hours, not paying attention to how tired we are, or how unhappy scrolling makes us feel.”
5. Your to-do list is a space that needs clearing to enjoy rest.

If you are mentally running through your to-do list while you are trying to rest, that’s not rest. It’s work. Not to mention, if there are too many things on your to-do list, you may never take time to rest because you think you have to earn it by getting everything done. This will help you simplify your to-do list.
A weekly to-do list may help you be more realistic about what you can accomplish so you don’t end up rolling items over from day to day.
If it’s been a while since you benefitted from time to chill out or you aren’t sure how to do it, try one of these 7 restful practices.

Oh hi! I'm Courtney and I've been simplifying my life since 2010. I remove the things that remove me from life. Things like clutter, debt, alcohol, busyness and drama. Now I have time for the good stuff like peace, ease, creativity, laughter and love. Let's simplify together, not so we can have a simple life, but so we can have the life we really want.
